content.text: Types (named by position of tibia to femur)
: direct anterior impact to proximal tibia
: gross deformity, swelling, ecchymosis, inability to extend knee
proximal tibial fracture w/ extension into the joint
: forceful, direct blow to lateral knee
: pain, tenderness, swelling, inability to ambulate
: direct force (e.g., fall onto flexed knee)
: point tenderness of patella, swelling, limited knee extension w/ pain,
▪patellar displaced from trochlear groove of femur
: lateral force to patella produces discomfort or
(i.e., apply medial force to patella while extending knee),
▪︎tibial osteochondritis thought to arise from overuse
of quad muscle during period of growth
prominence, swelling, & tenderness to the anterior tibial tubercle
fragmentation & soft tissue swelling over tibial tuberosity
